Name of the Surah

• It is called al-Tur (Mount Sinai), because it opens with God's oath by al-Tur, which is the mountain upon which God spoke to Musa (peace be upon him).

Among the Surah's Objectives

• A warning that the punishment on the Day of Resurrection will certainly take place, through God's oath by a number of His creations to confirm this, and a depiction of the state of the criminals when they are driven to Hellfire and what they suffer there, contrasted with a description of the state of the people of Paradise and the various forms of honour that God has prepared for the believers.

• Consoling the Prophet (ﷺ) by refuting the claims of the polytheists about him, their attribution of forgery to the Qur'an, their challenge to produce something like it, and a response to a number of their falsehoods, such as their denial of the resurrection of creation, their claim of multiple gods, and their mockery of the threat of punishment.

[Tafsir]

God swears by al-Tur, which is the mountain upon which God, glory be to Him, spoke to Musa (peace be upon him); and by a written book, which is the Qur'an, in unfolded pages; and by the Bayt al-Ma'mur (the Frequented House) in the heavens, which is visited by the noble angels who circumambulate it constantly; and by the raised canopy, which is the lowest heaven; and by the surging sea, filled with water.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 52, verse 7–10:

Indeed, the punishment of your Lord, O Messenger, upon the disbelievers is certainly going to occur. There is none that can prevent it when it occurs, on the day when the sky will shake and its order will be disrupted and its parts will be convulsed; and that will be at the end of the worldly life. The mountains will be removed from their places and will move like the moving of clouds.

Commentary of the King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 52, verses 13–14:

On the Day when these deniers are pushed violently and humiliatingly into the Fire of Hell, it will be said to them as a rebuke: "This is the Fire that you used to deny."

Commentary of the King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 52, verses 13–14:

On the Day when these deniers are pushed violently and humiliatingly into the Fire of Hell, it will be said to them as a rebuke: "This is the Fire that you used to deny."

Is this magic, or are you unable to see it? Taste the heat of this Fire. Endure its pain and its severity, or do not endure it. It makes no difference to you. You are only being repaid for what you used to do in the world.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 52, verse 19–20:

Translation of the Qur'anic verses (19–20):

﴿Eat and drink with pleasure, as a reward for what you used to do in the world of righteous deeds. They will recline on couches arranged in rows, and We will pair them with fair-complexioned women with wide, beautiful eyes.﴾

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 52, verse 19–20:

Translation of the Qur'anic verses (19–20):

﴿Eat and drink with pleasure, as a reward for what you used to do in the world of righteous deeds. They will recline on couches arranged in rows, and We will pair them with fair-complexioned women with wide, beautiful eyes.﴾

The Believers and their descendants who followed them in faith: We shall join their descendants with them, raising the descendants to their level in Paradise, even though the descendants did not reach their parents' deeds, so that the parents' eyes may be delighted by their children being with them in their dwellings. Thus they will be brought together in the best of states, and We shall not diminish anything of the reward of their deeds for them. Every person is held in pledge for what he has earned; no one bears the burden of another's sin.

We increased them with fruits and meats of whatever they desire and find delicious, among this bliss: they pass around in Paradise a cup of wine, one handing it to his companion, so that their joy is complete. This drink differs from the wine of this world: it does not take away the intellect of the one who drinks it, nor does it cause idle talk, nor is there in it any sinful or disobedient speech.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 52, verse 24:

And there will circulate among them young boys prepared for their service, who in their clearness, whiteness, and symmetry are like pearls kept safe in their shells.

The people of Paradise will turn to one another, asking about the great blessing they are in and its cause. They will say: "Indeed, we were before, in the world, among our families, fearful of our Lord, apprehensive of His punishment and retribution on the Day of Resurrection. So God bestowed His favor upon us with guidance and success, and protected us from the torment of the scorching wind of Hellfire (al-samum), which is its fire and its heat. Indeed, we used to supplicate to Him alone, not associating anything with Him, asking Him to protect us from the torment of the samum and to bring us to bliss. So He answered us and gave us what we asked, for He is the Most Kind (al-Barr), the Most Merciful (al-Rahim). Out of His kindness and mercy toward us, He granted us His good pleasure and Paradise, and protected us from His wrath and the Fire."

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 52, verse 29:

So remind them, O Messenger, with the Qur'an, those to whom you have been sent. You are not, by the grace of God upon you with prophethood and soundness of intellect, a soothsayer (kāhin) who reports the unseen without knowledge, nor a madman who does not comprehend what he says, as they claim.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 52, verses 30–31:

Or do the polytheists say, "He is a poet; we await for him the coming of death"? Say to them, [O Messenger]: "Wait for my death; indeed I am with you among those who wait, awaiting your punishment. And you will see to whom the final outcome belongs."

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 52, verses 30–31:

Or do the polytheists say, "He is a poet; we await for him the coming of death"? Say to them, [O Messenger]: "Wait for my death; indeed I am with you among those who wait, awaiting your punishment. And you will see to whom the final outcome belongs."

Rather, do their minds command them to this contradictory statement? That is because the attributes of soothsaying, poetry and madness cannot be combined at one time; rather, they are a people who exceed the limit in rebellion.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 52, verse 33:

﴿Or do they say, "He has invented it himself"? Rather, they do not believe. So if they believed, they would not have said what they said.﴾
Then let them produce a speech like the Qur'an, if they are truthful in their claim that Muhammad (ﷺ) invented it.

Were these polytheists created without any creator or originator for them, or are they the creators of themselves? Both of these possibilities are false and impossible. It is thus established that Allah, glorified is He, is the One who created them, and He alone deserves to be worshipped; nothing is fit for worship except Him.
Or did they create the heavens and the earth in this wondrous design? Rather, they have no certainty about God's punishment, so they are polytheists.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 52, verse 37:

Or do they have the treasuries of your Lord, so that they dispose of them? Or are they the overbearing controllers, dominating the creation of God by force and dominance? It is not so; rather, they are the helpless and weak.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 52, verse 38:

Or do they have a ladder to the heaven by which they listen to the revelation (that what they are upon is true)? Then let whoever claims that he has listened to that bring a clear proof that confirms his claim.

**Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 52, verse 39:**

Is it for Allah, glory be to Him, that there are daughters, and for you that there are sons, as you claim? It is a fabrication and a lie.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 52, verse 40:

Rather, O Messenger, do you ask these polytheists for a wage for conveying the message, so that they are burdened and weighed down by a debt you demand from them?

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 52, verse 41:

Or do they have knowledge of the unseen, so that they write it down and inform people of it? It is not so, for none knows the unseen in the heavens and the earth except Allah.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 52, verse 42:

Nay, they intend a plot against the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and the believers. But those who disbelieve, their scheme and plotting will rebound upon themselves.
Or do they have a deity other than Allah who deserves to be worshipped? Exalted is He above what they associate with Him. He has no partner in dominion, and no partner in His oneness and in worship.

Even if these polytheists were to see pieces of the sky falling upon them as a punishment, they would not move away from their denial, and they would say: "This is a cloud piled up, one part upon another."
So leave them, O Messenger, to their folly until they meet their Day, the Day on which they will be destroyed, which is the Day of Resurrection.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 52, verse 46:

On that Day, their scheming will not avail them anything against the punishment of Allah, nor will anyone be able to help them against the punishment of Allah.

Indeed, for these wrongdoers there is a punishment they will meet in this world before the punishment of the Day of Resurrection, such as killing and captivity, the punishment of the barzakh (the intermediate state between death and resurrection), and other things. But most of them do not know this.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 52, verses 48–49:

Be patient, O Messenger, with the decree of your Lord and His command concerning what He has entrusted you with of the message, and with the harm your people inflict on you. Indeed, you are under Our watch, protection and care. Glorify your Lord with His praise when you stand up for prayer, and when you rise from your sleep. And during the night, glorify Him with His praise and exalt Him, and pray to Him. Do this also at the time of Fajr prayer, at the time when the stars recede.

In this verse, the attribute of eyes is affirmed for Allah, the Exalted, in a manner befitting Him, without likening Him to His creation or describing the modality of His essence, glory be to Him and praise be to Him. This is established by the Sunnah (the prophetic tradition), and the early generations of the Ummah (salaf al-ummah, the righteous predecessors) agreed upon it. The word here is in the plural form to express magnification.
